title: Tensor cancellation across a pushout of ring sheaves
statement: Let $T$ be a topological space and $D,C,A,B$ sheaves of commutative rings on $T$. Suppose $r:D\to C$, $s:D\to A$, $b:C\to B$, $t:A\to B$ form a pushout in sheaves of commutative rings. For every sheaf of $A$-modules $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], there is a $C$-linear isomorphism $e_M:\operatorname{Res}_b(B\otimes_A M)\simeq C\otimes_D\operatorname{Res}_s M$, where the tensors are sheafified sectionwise tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and restrictions are [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For every $A$-linear map $a:M\to N$, $e_N\circ\operatorname{Res}_b(1\otimes a)=(1\otimes\operatorname{Res}_s a)\circ e_M$. On every open $W\subseteq T$ and every $m\in M(W)$, $e_M^{-1}(\theta_r(1\otimes m))=\theta_t(1\otimes m)$, with $\theta$ the corresponding sheafification unit.

proof.text: Construct the presheaf ring T(W)=C(W) tensor over D(W) with A(W). For any sheaf ring E, compatible maps C→E and A→E give the sectionwise map c tensor a ↦ u(c)v(a). It respects restrictions and extends uniquely to the sheafification of T. Conversely any map from that sheaf restricts to the compatible pair. Thus the sheafification is a pushout, hence isomorphic to B with its specified maps.

Let L be the sheafification of C tensor over D with Res_s M. The presheaf formula (c tensor a)(c′ tensor m)=cc′ tensor (a m) satisfies the balanced relations and commutes with restriction, so local representatives extend it to a B-action on L; the module laws are checked locally before sheafification. The A-linear map m↦θ(1 tensor m) extends B-linearly to β tensor m↦β·θ(1 tensor m). Its inverse as a C-linear sheaf map is obtained by sheafifying c tensor m↦b(c) tensor m. This map is D-balanced by the pushout-square equation. The first composite fixes c tensor m. Locally a section β of B is a sum of c tensor a; A-balancing identifies b(c)t(a) tensor m with b(c) tensor am, so the other composite fixes β tensor m. Both composites are identities by sheaf separation.

For a linear morphism M→N both comparisons apply that morphism only to the module tensor factor, so the naturality square commutes on local tensor generators and hence as sheaf maps. The inverse formula on 1 tensor m is θ(b(1) tensor m)=θ(1 tensor m). Zero rings, zero modules and the empty open require no separate nonvanishing assumptions.
